title: A vote on independence for Catalonia
detail: Negotiate a referendum on Catalonia's right to decide its future (*autodeterminació*), with international observers and with the EU and the Council of Europe helping both sides agree. The party cites advice from the Venice Commission and says it will stay pro-independence.
c: The Constitutional Court says that a referendum like this in one region goes against arts. 1.2 and 2 of the Constitution, because power belongs to all Spanish people together. It would first need a change to the Constitution under art. 168. Neither PSOE nor PP agrees. In our estimate, the EU and the Council of Europe will not help settle a dispute inside one country about its own Constitution.

s.t: Constitutional Court ruling 42/2014 on the Catalan sovereignty declaration (BOE)

title: A new funding model for Catalonia
detail: Use the funding model agreed with the government in January 2026 (*financiació singular*). Catalonia would collect all taxes and pay the state a share for its services. Under the "ordinality" rule (*ordinalitat*), a region that pays in more should not end up with less than regions that pay in less. The programme says Catalonia would get €4.7 billion more a year.
c: "Catalonia collects all taxes" is in practice the Basque *concierto*, which the Constitution allows only for the historic territories (first additional provision). It needs a change to the regional funding law LOFCA (176 votes) and probably to the Constitution. Other regions and PP are against it, and the Constitutional Court could cancel it.

s.t: Ley Orgánica 8/1980 on regional funding, LOFCA (BOE)

title: Cancel more than €17.1 billion of Catalan *FLA* debt
detail: Finish ERC's bill to cancel more than €17.1 billion that the Catalan government (Generalitat) owes to the state fund that lends to the regions (*FLA*). This would save about €1.5 billion a year in interest.
c: The bill to cancel €83 billion (€17.1 billion for Catalonia) went to parliament in December 2025. It is an organic law (176 votes), and Junts has not promised its support. Under a PP government, it will not happen.
pos: Catalonia pays less interest and can spend more on services, and the Generalitat's debt falls.
neg: Other regions will ask for the same, so state debt grows. It rewards the regions that borrowed more.

s.t: Finance Ministry, 9 Dec 2025: bill to write off €83,252 million of regional debt sent to parliament

title: Give Catalonia power over immigration and asylum
detail: Full power for Catalonia over immigration and asylum: receiving people, checking their needs and helping them settle. EU rules on sending people back would apply only with guarantees for their rights and with no automatic removals. A new asylum law with no processing of requests outside Spain.
c: Only the state has power over immigration (art. 149.1.2 of the Constitution). PSOE agreed with Junts to pass part of it to Catalonia under art. 150.2, but Congress said no on 23 September 2025 (173 for, 177 against). Border control cannot be passed to a region at all.

s.t: Congress record, 23 Sep 2025: delegation of immigration powers to Catalonia rejected (173 for, 177 against)

title: A Catalan rental law via art. 150.1 of the Constitution
detail: A state law under art. 150.1 of the Constitution that gives the Generalitat full power over rental law (*LAU*). The programme does not say what rent limits it wants.
c: Art. 150.1 allows the state to pass some law-making powers to a region. But civil law on rental contracts belongs to the state (art. 149.1.8), and lawyers disagree on whether such a transfer is allowed.

title: Higher taxes on homes nobody lives in; 21% VAT on tourist rentals
detail: Raise VAT and transfer tax (*ITP*) on homes bought for tourist or short-term rental, on second homes and on empty flats, and lower them for main homes. 21% VAT on tourist rentals, including through online platforms. Tax deductions for renovation, protected housing and saving energy.
c: 21% VAT on tourist rentals is realistic, because EU rules do not stop it. ITP is a regional tax, so Catalonia can raise it itself.
pos: It gives owners a reason to rent homes long-term again.
neg: Higher taxes on tourism, and it is not clear if more homes will be offered for rent.

s.t: Directive (EU) 2022/542 on VAT rates (BOE copy of the OJEU)

title: Tax on investment profits up to 35%; end the Beckham law
detail: Raise the top income tax rate on investment profits from 30% to 35%. Lower the rates on wages up to €35,000. Cut VAT on basic food and hygiene products. End the Beckham law (*Ley Beckham*: six years of paying tax as a non-resident) and the regime for international remote workers.
c: This matches PSOE (35% above €300,000). It is realistic with a left-wing majority.
pos: Lower tax on wages and higher tax on investment income: a fairer balance.
neg: It gives people a reason to move their money into holding companies or abroad.

title: A Catalan minimum wage of €1,460
detail: Give the Generalitat the power to set a Catalan minimum wage (*SMC*) of €1,460, and raise the state minimum wage (*SMI*) to 60% of the average gross wage, as the European Social Charter asks.
c: Only the state makes labour law (art. 149.1.7 of the Constitution). A regional minimum wage needs a change to the Workers' Statute and would probably be challenged in court.
